messages:
maria: Heads up — my log scraper picked up a wrapped Vault token in our partner webhook logs (redacted here). Not in prod prod, but looks valid and scoped to staging storage. Sharing minimal details until we confirm impact. @jamal @alex
jamal: Link? can you drop the log snippet and the blob id so I can check whether it was exfiltrated?
sec-bot: [alert] token-scanner v2 flagged base64 blob: <redacted> — match confidence 92% to vault-token pattern.
maria: Link: https://staging-logs.internal/ingest/2025/03/17/evt-98123 (internal only). Blob id ends with ...7f4. I ran `vault token lookup` with the accessor — it returns valid and TTL ~22h.
alex: If it's a Vault token, we need immediate containment. Is it a wrapped token (response-wrapping) or an actual client token?
maria: It's a client token — the partner's integration used a long-lived service token to fetch secrets and that token got logged by mistake during a retry path.
olivia: I'll take immediate revocation. Steps: 1) revoke token accessor 2) rotate the service SA key 3) enable additional audit logging for the vault-proxy path. I'm on it, ETA 15m.
jamal: For rotation: do we rotate KMS wrapping key or just rewrap the leaked artifacts? If the partner used KMS-wrapped ciphertext we should rewrap and rotate the wrapping key to avoid replay.
alex: Good call. Short-term: revoke token + delete SA key. Mid-term: rotate KMS key and rewrap secrets. Also add RBAC lock: restrict the partner SA to the narrower bucket prefix.
olivia: Executing now:
```
# revoke token by accessor
vault token-revoke -accessor hDk7...7f4
# delete SA key (gcloud)
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=svc-partner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Done. Token revoke confirmed.
jamal: I'll run a quick audit to see whether that accessor was used from other IPs. Also will search logs for similar base64 patterns in the last 30 days.
maria: Thanks. Note: partner said their CI pushed logs to a central blobstore during an outage window — likely paste of wrapped token got copied into partner logs. We'll coordinate with partner to hard-delete those objects.
sec-bot: [audit] scheduled: create new audit backend for vault-proxy (enable file and syslog sinks, 90d retention), ticket #SEC-4821 created.
alex: After revoke/keys deleted, next actions: 1) partner to purge logged blobs (maria to coordinate), 2) rotate wrapping KMS key (jamal + infra), 3) run a full SCAN for any other leaked tokens, 4) RBAC tighten on partner SA, 5) add pre-commit linting to partner integration to prevent logging secrets.
maria: I'll own coordination with partner and share deletion receipts. Jamal, please own KMS key rotation plan and timeline. Olivia — can you confirm the vault audit backend config change and post the diff?
olivia: Will do, posting diff in 10m. Quick note: to avoid breaking clients, we'll create a new KMS key version, rewrap secrets, then promote and retire old key version.
jamal: Ack. Tentative timeline: rotate wrapping key within 48h, rewrap backlog in first 24h after key creation, full audit scan in 72h. If we find other live tokens, escalate to incident.
alex: Also add an RBAC rule: deny iam.serviceAccounts.keys.create for partner org except via onboarding pipeline. I'll open a policy PR.
maria: Closing loop: partner committed to immediate blob deletion and CI change. Keeping thread updated. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
